title: Radiological and clinical outcomes after cervical spine cage implantation: comparison of uncoated and unfilled PEEK cages vs. titanium-coated and filled PEEK cages.
summary:
The further development of medical devices requires the follow-up and comparison of the results of older and newer products.
The further development of the so-called cages (machine-shaped placeholders for the intervertebral space) lies in an added titanium coating and in an additional filling of the cavity from ceramic bone substitute and autologous bone material.
All patients who have been treated with unfilled and uncoated as well as filled and coated cages in the orthopedics department of the MHH at the Diakovere Annastift since 2005 are now to be interviewed, and the available data and X-ray images are to be evaluated.
The main focus will be on the radiological results regarding bony consolidation (growing together), but also on the documentation of complications, daily functions, psychological self-assessment and pain data.
As part of the study, study participants will be asked to complete questionnaires. In addition, radiographs and findings will be evaluated.
conditions: Osteochondrosis of the spine in adults : Cervical region

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- all patients who have been treated at Annastift Hannover by Prof. Daentzer since 01.01.2005 by means of implantation of a PEEK cage or titanium-coated and filled PEEK cages with corresponding indication
- Patients with a fusion at several heights
Exclusion criteria:
- Application of an additional plate at the same cervical height for further stabilization.
